findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime keys
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies Paginator.get_item_key, which does `int(math.floor(value))` on the sort-key attribute. The endpoint uses it with order_by="-datetime", so `value` is a datetime, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError. Every paginated request to the audit-log endpoint with optimized_pagination=true will fail with a 500. It needed the DateTimePaginator-style conversion (strftime-based ms conversion) like DateTimePaginator.get_item_key/value_from_cursor.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing of a Django QuerySet raises an error
findings.body: The 'advanced feature' path slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly does not support negative indices and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (in newer Django, ValueError). So the advertised negative-offset pagination never works; any client sending a cursor with a negative offset to the optimized path gets a 500, not 'efficient reverse pagination'. The comment claiming the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually wrong.

findings.title: value_from_cursor is incompatible with the DateTimePaginator cursors used by this endpoint
findings.body: DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor converts the millisecond cursor value back into a UTC datetime before it is injected into the SQL where-clause in build_queryset. OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value (an int/float). When used with the '-datetime' ordering in the audit-log endpoint, a client-supplied cursor value (e.g. 1718000000000) is compared directly against a timestamp column, so results are wrong or the query errors depending on the database. Cursours produced by one paginator are also silently consumed by the other depending on the caller's permissions, so paging behavior differs per user for the same cursor.

findings.title: Undocumented query param silently changes pagination semantics per user
findings.body: The new `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter is not part of the documented API (publish status EXPERIMENTAL aside) and switches the endpoint to a paginator with a different cursor value encoding, and only for superusers or users with global access. The same `cursor` string therefore yields different (or broken) results depending on who sends it, and clients cannot rely on the cursor format being stable across pages if a user's permissions change. There is no serialization/test coverage for this alternate response path.

findings.title: BasePaginator change silently rewrites invalid cursors to page 1 for non-prev cursors
findings.body: The rewritten slicing logic `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors. Previously a malformed cursor with a negative offset produced a (wrong but detectable) slice; now it silently returns the first page while the next/prev cursor computation in build_cursor still uses the original negative offset (e.g. `_build_next_values` computes `next_offset = offset + limit` from the raw offset), producing cursors that are internally inconsistent with the rows actually returned. For is_prev cursors the negative offset is still passed through, where Django raises on negative slicing. The change also alters behavior for all existing endpoints using BasePaginator, not just audit logs.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but no validation or support was added
findings.body: The added comment in Cursor.__init__ says negative offsets are now allowed as a 'performance optimization', but the code is unchanged: Cursor.from_string already accepted any int, and nothing in this file handles negative offsets. The comment misleads readers into thinking negative-offset cursors are a supported, working feature; downstream, Django queryset slicing will actually reject them. Comments-only changes that assert unsupported behavior should not be merged.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the modified BasePaginator slicing
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, a new constructor flag (enable_advanced_features), and modifies the core slicing logic of BasePaginator.get_result used by many endpoints, but includes no tests. At minimum there should be tests covering: datetime keys, negative offsets (which would have caught the math.floor(TypeError) and Django negative-slice failures), prev/next cursor round-trips, and the audit-log endpoint's two code paths.
